{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 190,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Shared variables are written concurrently in search init",
      "body": "In searchSupport.init, each errgroup goroutine assigns to the outer err variable and increments totalBatchesIndexed without synchronization. This is a data race: the stored error and counter are nondeterministic, and race-detector runs will fail. Use a local error per goroutine and an atomic counter or channel."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 203,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Initial index build can miss writes that occur while building",
      "body": "searchSupport.init builds indexes first and discards the resource version returned by build, then calls WatchWriteEvents after all builds are complete. The watch starts from the latest resource version at that later time, so writes that happen during the potentially long initial build are not applied to the new indexes. This can leave search results stale until affected resources are written again. Start watching before building or backfill events from the RV returned by build."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 209,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Watch event goroutine does not handle a closed events channel",
      "body": "The goroutine in searchSupport.init receives from events with a single-value receive and ignores whether the channel is closed. If the storage backend closes the channel, the loop receives nil events forever and handleEvent will dereference a nil *WrittenEvent, causing a panic or tight loop. Use v, ok := <-events and return when !ok, and select on a cancellable context."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 202,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Search watcher is started with an uncancellable background context",
      "body": "searchSupport.init creates watchctx := context.Background() and starts an event-processing goroutine with no way to stop it. server.Stop cancels the server context but does not cancel this context, so the goroutine can leak, especially in tests or when resource servers are recreated. Use a cancellable context tied to the server lifecycle."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 263,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "IndexMetrics is used without nil checks in event handling",
      "body": "handleEvent updates IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds for ADDED and DELETED events without checking whether IndexMetrics is nil, while other code paths in the same file guard with if IndexMetrics != nil. If metrics are not initialized, the first watch event will panic. Add nil checks or ensure metrics are always initialized."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 925,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "History and Origin can panic when search is not configured",
      "body": "server.History and server.Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. server.Search performs this check, but History and Origin do not. If the resource server is created without search support and these gRPC methods are called, the server will panic. Return a not-configured error when s.search is nil."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 510,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Update swallows backend read errors",
      "body": "In server.Update, if s.backend.ReadResource returns a response with Error set, the method returns an empty UpdateResponse and a nil error without setting rsp.Error. Clients cannot distinguish a backend failure from a successful response with no data. Propagate the backend error in rsp.Error or return an error."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 258,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Constructor does not clean up when Init fails",
      "body": "NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context and may initialize lifecycle/search state, but if s.Init fails it returns without calling cancel or stopping lifecycle hooks. This can leak goroutines or backend resources during failed startups or in tests. Call cancel and appropriate cleanup before returning the error."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 88,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "BuildIndex no longer serializes builds for the same index key",
      "body": "The global cache lock was removed from bleveBackend.BuildIndex, and only the final cache insertion is locked. searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex has no single-flight or per-key lock, so concurrent requests for a missing index can call BuildIndex for the same NamespacedResource simultaneously. This can create duplicate memory indexes, concurrently open or write the same file-based directory, and overwrite the cache entry, causing wasted work, leaks, or corrupted indexes. Add per-key locking or single-flight semantics."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 146,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "TotalDocs iterates cache without holding cacheMu",
      "body": "bleveBackend.TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu.RLock, while BuildIndex writes to b.cache under cacheMu.Lock. Concurrent map reads and writes can panic or return inconsistent counts. Add a read lock around the iteration."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 138,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Replacing a cache entry does not close the previous index",
      "body": "BuildIndex assigns the newly built bleveIndex into b.cache without closing any existing index for the same key. If a rebuild or a concurrent build race replaces an entry, the old bleve.Index remains open, leaking memory/file handles and possibly retaining locks on file-based indexes. Close or remove old indexes when replacing cache entries."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go",
      "line": 584,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Poller span is not ended when listLatestRVs fails",
      "body": "In backend.poller, a span is started for each poll tick. If b.listLatestRVs returns an error, the code logs and continues without calling span.End(), leaking tracing state. End the span before continuing, for example with defer or an explicit span.End()."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go",
      "line": 126,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "Span name has a doubled dot",
      "body": "GetResourceStats creates a span with tracePrefix + '.GetResourceStats' while tracePrefix already ends with a dot, producing 'sql.resource..GetResourceStats'. Use tracePrefix + 'GetResourceStats' or adjust the prefix."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Shared variables are written concurrently in search init
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, each errgroup goroutine assigns to the outer err variable and increments totalBatchesIndexed without synchronization. This is a data race: the stored error and counter are nondeterministic, and race-detector runs will fail. Use a local error per goroutine and an atomic counter or channel.

findings.title: Initial index build can miss writes that occur while building
findings.body: searchSupport.init builds indexes first and discards the resource version returned by build, then calls WatchWriteEvents after all builds are complete. The watch starts from the latest resource version at that later time, so writes that happen during the potentially long initial build are not applied to the new indexes. This can leave search results stale until affected resources are written again. Start watching before building or backfill events from the RV returned by build.

findings.title: Watch event goroutine does not handle a closed events channel
findings.body: The goroutine in searchSupport.init receives from events with a single-value receive and ignores whether the channel is closed. If the storage backend closes the channel, the loop receives nil events forever and handleEvent will dereference a nil *WrittenEvent, causing a panic or tight loop. Use v, ok := <-events and return when !ok, and select on a cancellable context.

findings.title: Search watcher is started with an uncancellable background context
findings.body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx := context.Background() and starts an event-processing goroutine with no way to stop it. server.Stop cancels the server context but does not cancel this context, so the goroutine can leak, especially in tests or when resource servers are recreated. Use a cancellable context tied to the server lifecycle.

findings.title: IndexMetrics is used without nil checks in event handling
findings.body: handleEvent updates IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds for ADDED and DELETED events without checking whether IndexMetrics is nil, while other code paths in the same file guard with if IndexMetrics != nil. If metrics are not initialized, the first watch event will panic. Add nil checks or ensure metrics are always initialized.

findings.title: History and Origin can panic when search is not configured
findings.body: server.History and server.Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. server.Search performs this check, but History and Origin do not. If the resource server is created without search support and these gRPC methods are called, the server will panic. Return a not-configured error when s.search is nil.

findings.title: Update swallows backend read errors
findings.body: In server.Update, if s.backend.ReadResource returns a response with Error set, the method returns an empty UpdateResponse and a nil error without setting rsp.Error. Clients cannot distinguish a backend failure from a successful response with no data. Propagate the backend error in rsp.Error or return an error.

findings.title: Constructor does not clean up when Init fails
findings.body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context and may initialize lifecycle/search state, but if s.Init fails it returns without calling cancel or stopping lifecycle hooks. This can leak goroutines or backend resources during failed startups or in tests. Call cancel and appropriate cleanup before returning the error.

findings.title: BuildIndex no longer serializes builds for the same index key
findings.body: The global cache lock was removed from bleveBackend.BuildIndex, and only the final cache insertion is locked. searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex has no single-flight or per-key lock, so concurrent requests for a missing index can call BuildIndex for the same NamespacedResource simultaneously. This can create duplicate memory indexes, concurrently open or write the same file-based directory, and overwrite the cache entry, causing wasted work, leaks, or corrupted indexes. Add per-key locking or single-flight semantics.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu.RLock, while BuildIndex writes to b.cache under cacheMu.Lock. Concurrent map reads and writes can panic or return inconsistent counts. Add a read lock around the iteration.

findings.title: Replacing a cache entry does not close the previous index
findings.body: BuildIndex assigns the newly built bleveIndex into b.cache without closing any existing index for the same key. If a rebuild or a concurrent build race replaces an entry, the old bleve.Index remains open, leaking memory/file handles and possibly retaining locks on file-based indexes. Close or remove old indexes when replacing cache entries.

findings.title: Poller span is not ended when listLatestRVs fails
findings.body: In backend.poller, a span is started for each poll tick. If b.listLatestRVs returns an error, the code logs and continues without calling span.End(), leaking tracing state. End the span before continuing, for example with defer or an explicit span.End().

findings.title: Span name has a doubled dot
findings.body: GetResourceStats creates a span with tracePrefix + '.GetResourceStats' while tracePrefix already ends with a dot, producing 'sql.resource..GetResourceStats'. Use tracePrefix + 'GetResourceStats' or adjust the prefix.
